source.title: Neuro-MoBRE: Exploring Multi-subject Multi-task Intracranial Decoding via Explicit Heterogeneity Resolving
source.authors: Di Wu; Yifei Jia; Si-Yuan Li; Shi-Qi Zhao; Jie Yang; M. Sawan

record.file_problem: No apparent file problem; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses whether neural-decoding models inherit NLP scaling benefits and reports an architecture-size ablation, but it does not test the claim's held-out language-model loss laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and argues that simply increasing parameters and data does not necessarily reproduce NLP scaling successes in neurophysiological decoding. Appendix H.1 reports decoding accuracy for four Neuro-MoBRE architecture configurations. These are not measurements of held-out cross-entropy loss, power-law fits, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocations. The accuracy results are recorded as related findings, not as results for a claim version.
record.test_reason: A neural-decoding methods paper. It cites Kaplan et al. and argues that naive scaling of neurophysiological models fails. Its only scaling evidence is a four-configuration architecture ablation (Appendix H.1, Table A3) reporting classification accuracy. There is no loss measurement, no power-law fit, no extrapolation and no compute allocation. The results do not bear on any version, including V5, which requires a power-law form in another modality.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The paper's main conclusion is that Neuro-MoBRE, by explicitly resolving subject and task heterogeneity, outperforms prior decoders on 11 subjects and five tasks. The scaling ablation is secondary. The authors say modest depth/width increases improve accuracy, though one task (seizure detection at 4-128) actually dips. They say 16-512 collapses, likely from insufficient data, so very large models are not needed.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies intracranial neural decoding, not language-model pretraining loss scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Decoder depth and embedding dimension vary in Appendix H.1; the largest tested configuration performs worse.

fits_no_version.finding: Neuro-MoBRE on sEEG decoding: 4-128 and 8-64 give small accuracy changes versus 4-64 (mostly up, except 4-128 seizure detection). 16-512 drops on all five tasks, e.g. initial decoding 0.2826 to 0.1597. The authors attribute the drop to insufficient data for the parameter count.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small-data neural-decoding setups, increasing model size without more data can degrade task accuracy rather than improve it.

record.problems: The architecture-size ablation reports decoding accuracy rather than held-out loss, tests only four configurations, gives no parameter counts or uncertainty estimates for these results, and does not fit or compare scaling curves.

untested.parts: No held-out language-model loss over parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fit used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters versus tokens.
No depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count. The configurations change total size, and parameter counts are not given.
Sizes are varied in a neural-decoding model, but no power-law fit or loss curve is reported. Four points of accuracy cannot show the form.
No language-model downstream tasks against scale or loss.
No fitted exponents or fitting-choice analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (discusses) and tranche (T6) are correct. The Kaplan citation is motivational only. Table A3 values match the text. The 4-64 rows duplicate the main-result numbers from Tables 1 and 2.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run loss fit or prediction of larger language-model runs.
No fixed-compute search over parameter and token allocations.
No comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count using language-model loss.
The study varies neural-decoder architecture size and reports decoding accuracy, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.
No downstream language-model task performance measured against scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents, power-law curve comparisons, or analysis of fitting choices for the claimed scaling laws.
